message.content:
Here’s a quick, copy‑and‑paste‑ready example of how you can pull just the **ID** and **context** fields for community comments on `test4.org`, using your continuation cursor (`cur456`) and API key (`key123`).

---

## 1. Build the request URL

```http
GET https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments
```

### Query parameters

| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `domain`  | `test4.org` | Target domain |
| `fields`  | `id,context` | Tell the API to return only the `id` and `context` attributes |
| `cursor`  | `cur456` | Pagination cursor to continue from the last batch |
| `api_key` | `key123` | Your authentication key |

### Full URL

```
https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments?domain=test4.org&fields=id,context&cursor=cur456&api_key=key123
```

---

## 2. Make the HTTP request

You can use `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client in your preferred language.

### Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments?domain=test4.org&fields=id,context&cursor=cur456&api_key=key123"
```

### Using Python (`requests`)

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments"
params = {
    "domain": "test4.org",
    "fields": "id,context",
    "cursor": "cur456",
    "api_key": "key123"
}

response = requests.get(url, params=params)
data = response.json()
print(data)
```

---

## 3. Expected JSON response

```json
{
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "cmt_001",
      "context": {
        "author": "alice",
        "text": "Great post!",
        "timestamp": "2024-11-10T12:34:56Z"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "cmt_002",
      "context": {
        "author": "bob",
        "text": "I disagree.",
        "timestamp": "2024-11-10T13:01:22Z"
      }
    }
    // … more comments
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cur789"   // if there are more pages
}
```

> **Tip:**  
> *If you only need the raw IDs (no context), set `fields=id` instead.*  
> *If you want to keep the cursor for the next page, look for the `next_cursor` field in the response.*

---

## 4. Handling pagination

If the response contains a `next_cursor`, repeat the same request with that cursor:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments?domain=test4.org&fields=id,context&cursor=cur789&api_key=key123"
```

Continue until `next_cursor` is absent or empty.

---

That’s all you need! Just replace the placeholder URL (`https://api.yourservice.com/v1/comments`) with the actual endpoint of your service, and you’re good to go.
